correctness.rationale: For t and p arbitrary, the three Kraus unitaries commute because all spatial shifts are global, giving exact independent binomial quantum-step count and symmetric random translations. The coherent Fourier symbol has smooth isolated eigenvalues for 0<theta<pi/2; changing variables in its weighted velocity law yields the normalized Konno density. The three probability regimes follow from binomial concentration and classical CLT; for finite positive lambda, characteristic functions factor and produce Gaussian plus lambda*Konno. Exact integration gives second moment 1-s and fourth moment 1-3s/2+s^3/2, hence strictly negative fourth cumulant. Boundary p=1 and p=0, lambda=0 and infinity, were separately checked. Numerically, an independent finite Kraus density-matrix propagation agrees with the exact convolution (270 channel/normalization/symmetry checks), and 27 additional coherent/critical moment checks passed. Finite tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: The natural, physically observable boundary between classical diffusion and residual coherent ballistic spreading is singular as the classical-step probability tends to one. The theorem quantifies that boundary at coherent-step probability proportional to inverse square-root observation time, identifies its entire one-parameter non-Gaussian density family and a strictly negative cumulant diagnostic, and provides an exact finite-time simulation reduction. The result is not merely a renaming of the already known Konno distribution or a fixed-p variance: it classifies a previously unaddressed singular regime of a published quantum stochastic channel. It does not claim a new quantum algorithm, finite-time local limit, or monitored-return law.
